root_cause.text: The `ns_name` pointer is assigned from `ent->ns_name` without nullifying the source pointer, causing the same memory address to be freed twice—once through `aa_load_ent_free(ent)` and again through `kfree(ns_name)`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that after the assignment `ns_name = ent->ns_name;` at line 1095, the fix adds `ent->ns_name = NULL;` to prevent the double-free. Without this nullification, when `aa_load_ent_free(ent)` is called at line 1262, it frees the memory pointed to by `ent->ns_name`, and then `kfree(ns_name)` at line 1270 attempts to free the same memory address again, resulting in a use-after-free/double-free vulnerability.

bic_trace_step.reason: At line 850, `ns_name = ent->ns_name;` assigns the pointer from `ent->ns_name` directly to the local variable `ns_name` without nullifying the source. This creates a double-free vulnerability because: (1) `ns_name` is used later in the function (lines 854-863, 994, 1005) and is expected to be freed by the caller, and (2) when `aa_load_ent_free(ent)` is called at lines 977 and 1010, it will free the same memory address that `ns_name` points to. The vulnerability manifests when the function exits via the `fail` label (line 993) or completes normally (line 981), as `ns_name` will reference freed memory from `ent->ns_name` that was already deallocated by `aa_load_ent_free(ent)`. The fix would require either: (a) nullifying `ent->ns_name` after assignment, or (b) duplicating the string instead of copying the pointer.
